params.body:
> **Read this first: the server probably needs one package.** HEIC decoding is not something PHP
> can do on its own. On the Forge box, check what is there:
>
> ```bash
> php -r 'echo extension_loaded("imagick") ? implode(",", Imagick::queryFormats("HEI*")) : "no imagick"; echo PHP_EOL;'
> which heif-convert magick convert
> ```
>
> If that prints `no imagick` (or an imagick without `HEIC`/`HEIF` in the list) **and** none of the
> binaries is found, install the CLI decoder and restart php-fpm:
>
> ```bash
> sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libheif1 libheif-examples
> sudo service php8.4-fpm restart   # or the version the site runs
> ```
>
> `libheif-examples` is what carries `heif-convert`; `libheif1` alone is not enough. Nothing in this
> pull request breaks without it: the uploader then refuses HEIC with a translated message telling
> the dealer to set the iPhone camera to "Most Compatible". After the install, HEIC simply starts
> working, with no deploy. `php artisan stocklist:smoke heic` says which of the two situations the
> box is in, in one line.

## Why

A dealer whose iPhone is set to "High Efficiency" shoots HEIC/HEIF, and the platform accepted none
of it: the uploader rejected the type client-side, and had it got through, the browser cannot
decode HEIC (so it cannot resize it either) and GD cannot read it, so Intervention would have
thrown deep inside a queued job — a photo that never appears, without anyone being told why. There
was not a single reference to `heic` or `heif` in the repository.

## Where the conversion happens

**Server-side, at the door, before anything else touches the file.** `App\Support\UploadedImage` is
the single point every upload passes through; from there on nothing downstream knows a HEIC ever
existed. The converted file is a JPEG with the same base name, so `car_image_{sort_order}`,
`media_version`, `media_set` and the derived sizes from `VehicleImageService` are all reached along
the path that already existed. No change to `ProcessVehiclePhoto` or to the photo pipeline.

Why not client-side: the browser has no HEIC decoder, so `createImageBitmap` fails. `SlUpload` keeps
its resize for JPEG/PNG/WebP and deliberately leaves HEIC alone; the original travels (2 to 5 MB,
one file per request — see below) and the server resizes it as it always did.

Which converter is used is a property of the machine, not of this code, so it is probed rather than
assumed. `App\Support\HeicConverter` tries, in order: **imagick** built against libheif
(`Imagick::queryFormats('HEI*')`), **php-vips**, the **`heif-convert`** CLI, **ImageMagick's CLI**
with a HEIC delegate. `config('features.heic_converter')` (`HEIC_CONVERTER`) can force one or turn
the whole thing off with `none`.

Which driver Intervention itself uses: there is no `config/image.php`, so intervention/image 2.x
runs on its default, **GD** — and GD cannot read HEIC at any version. That is why the conversion
happens outside Intervention and hands it a JPEG.

If no converter is present, nothing is faked: the upload is refused with
`photos.heic_unsupported` (NL/FR/EN/DE, the languages `resources/lang` carries), which names the
iPhone setting to change. A refused upload with a reason beats a photo that silently disappears.

**Orientation.** HEIC carries EXIF rotation, and the existing pipeline handles none: there is no
`orientate()` anywhere in `app/`, and JPEGs only come out upright because the client-side canvas
resize normalises them. So the converter does it itself: imagick uses `autoOrient()` and stamps
`ORIENTATION_TOPLEFT`, vips uses `autorot()`, magick uses `-auto-orient`, and `heif-convert` (which
copies the EXIF across without touching the pixels) gets a follow-up pass through
`Image::make()->orientate()`. The JPEG that leaves the door is upright, tag and pixels agreeing.

## Server requirements

| what | where | needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `libheif1` + `libheif-examples` (gives `heif-convert`) | Forge box, apt | the cheapest route; nothing to rebuild |
| or `imagick` built against libheif | Forge box, apt/pecl | also fine, and then Intervention could be pointed at it later |
| or `php-vips` | composer + libvips with heif | fine, not currently in `composer.json` |

`php artisan stocklist:smoke heic` (also part of `--all`) reports which one the box uses, or says it
has none and prints the install command. It is a `–` (skip), not a `✗`: a missing decoder is a gap,
not an outage, and should not turn the cutover smoke run red.

## Upload limits

I could not read the box's php.ini or nginx config from here, so this is what to verify rather than
what I measured:

```bash
php -i | grep -E 'post_max_size|upload_max_filesize'
grep -r client_max_body_size /etc/nginx/
```

What the repository does pin: `SlUpload` has `maxBytes: 20 * 1024 * 1024` and refuses anything
larger locally, before it leaves the phone; `ValidatePostSize` (in `app/Http/Kernel.php`) turns an
over-`post_max_size` request into a 413, which `SlUpload` already translates into "too large".

The important bit for "a handful of HEIC photos at once": **`SlUpload` uploads one file per
request**, sequentially (`processQueue` sends the next only after the previous finishes). Ten photos
are ten requests, so the ceiling that matters is one HEIC of 2 to 5 MB plus form overhead, not the
sum. Forge's stock php.ini leaves `upload_max_filesize`/`post_max_size` well above that, and
`client_max_body_size` in Forge's nginx template likewise — but run the two commands above before
the cutover and raise them to at least `32M` if they are lower, since an unresized HEIC is now the
largest thing the photo tile sends.

## What was covered

Checked each upload path that a dealer can feed from a phone:

| path | route / entry | covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vehicle photos | `ownvehicle.update.dropzone` → `ProcessVehiclePhoto` | yes, `UploadedImage::photo()` |
| Damage photos (tile) | `ownvehicle.update.damagedropzone` | yes, `UploadedImage::photo()`, before the damage record is created |
| Damage photos (form array) | `App\Http\Helpers\Photo::upload_image_by_name` | yes, `UploadedImage::normaliseAll()` |
| Dealer logo | `DealerController::upload` (`image`) | yes, `UploadedImage::normalise()` |
| Showroom backgrounds | `SettingsController::saveBackgroundFile` | yes, `UploadedImage::normalise()` |
| User avatar | `UserController::upload` (`image`) | yes, `UploadedImage::normalise()` |
| Brand/category images | `SimpleController::upload` | yes, `normalise()`; an SVG stays an SVG |
| RealGarant maintenance history | `OrderController::uploadContractFiles` | yes, `normaliseAll()`; a PDF stays a PDF (this one is photographed with a phone and sent on to a third party, so a HEIC there was unreadable at the other end too) |
| Dealer PDF attachment | `DealerController::upload` (`attachment`) | not applicable, PDF only |
| Photo crop/edit modal | `editImageModal` | not applicable, works on an image already stored |

Client side (`resources/views/partials/ui-upload.blade.php`, the shared `SlUpload`):

- `image/heic` and `image/heif` added to the default accept list and to the five call sites, plus
  the matching extensions on the `<input accept>` so the iOS picker does not grey the files out.
- The type check now falls back to the extension when the browser gives no mime type — iOS hands
  over a `.HEIC` with an empty `type` often enough that name-blindness alone would keep the refusal.
- The "only JPG, PNG or WebP" message is now built from the accept list, so it tells the truth per
  uploader (the RealGarant one accepts PDF and used to claim otherwise).
- No `objectURL` preview for a HEIC: the browser cannot paint it, and a broken tile reads as a
  failed upload.
- The resize path is unchanged and still skips HEIC, with the reason written down next to it.

**No type check was weakened.** The opposite: `UploadedImage::photo()` now refuses anything that is
not a JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF on the two photo routes with a translated 422, where a PDF dropped on the
photo tile previously became a 500 from `Image::make` inside a queued job.
`UnsupportedImageException` is in `Handler::$dontReport`, so a dealer picking the wrong file no
longer mails an error report.

## Checked

- `php artisan test --filter='Photo|Image|Vehicle|Upload|SmokeTest|DemoMedia'` — 18 passed, 0
  failed, 1554 assertions (the "warnings" are a pre-existing `file_get_contents` notice from the
  worktree having no `.env`; `VehicleImageRouteTest` shows the same on an untouched checkout).
- Also ran `StylesheetSyntax|UiApiUsage|RulesCoverage|BuildContract` alongside: green.
- New: `tests/Feature/HeicUploadTest.php` — six tests. A HEIC posted to the upload route reaches the
  converter, comes out as `{id}/car_image_{sort}.jpg`, is really a JPEG in the bucket, has its
  `media_version` and `media_set`, and leaves nothing behind in the tmp drop folder; a HEIC with no
  mime type is still recognised by its `ftyp` brand; a server without a converter answers 422 with
  the message naming the iPhone setting and creates no half record; an unsupported type (PDF) gets
  its own 422; an ordinary JPEG never touches the converter; and a `.MOV` from the same phone (same
  box structure, different brand) is not mistaken for a photo.
- **The converter itself is stubbed in the tests, deliberately and stated here**: CI has gd and
  exif, no imagick-with-libheif and no `heif-convert`, so a real HEIC could not be decoded there at
  all. What the tests do exercise for real is the routing decision — recognition, the hand-off, the
  path afterwards, and both refusals. The four converter backends are exercised by
  `stocklist:smoke heic` on a machine that has one.
- No JS in `resources/js` changed (the uploader is an inline blade script), so `public/build` is
  untouched and uncommitted.
params.title: Photos: accept HEIC from a phone
